gloss: cannot bear to watch; too painful to see

definitions.gloss: cannot bear to watch; too painful to see; unbearable to look at
definitions.explanation: Describes a situation so pitiful, painful, or distressing that one cannot stand to keep watching. Expresses deep sympathy or discomfort at someone else's suffering or a deteriorating situation.

examples.japanese: {見|み}るに{忍|しの}びない{光景|こうけい}だった。
examples.english: It was a scene too painful to watch.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{落|お}ち{込|こ}む{姿|すがた}は{見|み}るに{忍|しの}びなかった。
examples.english: His dejected appearance was unbearable to watch.

examples.japanese: {荒|あ}れ{果|は}てた{故郷|ふるさと}の{姿|すがた}は、{見|み}るに{忍|しの}びないものだった。
examples.english: The sight of my devastated hometown was too painful to bear.

notes:
USAGE:
{忍|しの}ぶ means "to endure" or "to bear," and {忍|しの}びない is its negative potential form meaning "cannot bear." The expression is literary and somewhat formal, often used in writing and emotional descriptions. It conveys strong empathy or distress.

Variation: {見|み}るに{堪|た}えない is a similar expression with a slightly different nuance — it can mean either "too painful to watch" (like this expression) or "too poor in quality to watch."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見|み}るに{忍|しの}びない{光景|こうけい} (a scene too painful to watch)
- {見|み}るに{忍|しの}びない{姿|すがた} (an unbearable sight)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見|み}るに{堪|た}えない: cannot bear to watch — similar but can also mean "unwatchable" due to poor quality
- {目|め}を{覆|おお}う: to cover one's eyes — a more vivid physical expression of the same feeling
